title: What can physical AI actually do on the factory floor?
summary: After visiting a new deployment and IMTS in Chicago — the largest manufacturing technology show in North America — Professor Sentance asks what physical AI can really do in a factory. A century of process engineering has been about removing variation, he argues, so AI’s great strength — adapting to the unfamiliar — adds little to today’s linear production lines. The real opportunity lies in the adaptive, non-linear processes that manufacturers abandoned because they were too unpredictable to manage or too dangerous for people.

title: Finding causal relationships in incomplete data
summary: In “PAIR-CI: Calibrated Conditional Independence Testing for Causal Discovery with Incomplete Data”, Robinson and Lall introduce a machine learning method for uncovering causal relationships in data with missing values — a pervasive problem in the surveys, firm records, and cross-national datasets that social scientists rely on. Where existing approaches can mistake gaps in the data for genuine causal links, the new method keeps such false discoveries rare. The paper will appear at NeurIPS 2026, the premier venue for research in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

title: The Chain of Peace: Do Supply Chain Chokepoints Deter War?
summary: Advanced semiconductors cannot be made by any one country. Design software is American, lithography machines Dutch, optics German, photoresists Japanese, fabrication Taiwanese — and remove any node and the chain breaks. Pham and Scholten argue that this structure, not Taiwan's foundries alone, is what deters conflict in the Taiwan Strait, because a chip fab seized by force produces nothing without the network behind it. The uncomfortable implication is that export controls and reshoring, each sensible in isolation, are steadily dismantling the interdependence that keeps the peace.
